subject: Urgent: Montecure v4b quant profile causing elevated p99 latency and token errors
messages:
From: Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@montecure.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: anya@montecure.ai, support@montecure.ai
Date: Fri, 9 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe p99 latency + "token decode" errors since v4b + Q4 quant switch

Tessa / team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p99 latency and a growing number of token-decoding errors after the model upgrade you rolled yesterday (v4b with the Q4 quant profile). Impact: our checkout rejection rate spiked and overall throughput dropped ~20% during peak. Attached is a short sample (latency-sample-2027-05-09.csv) and an error trace.

Key points:
- Window started ~22:30 UTC on 2027-05-08 and is still ongoing
- p50 largely stable, p95 up ~30ms, p99 up ~420ms
- Intermittent "decode stall" errors in logs referencing token alignment failures
- Business impact: we estimate ~18% conversion loss in the last 3 hours

This is high-severity for our users. Pls advise immediate mitigation steps and whether you can roll us back to the previous variant. We are available on a call now.

- Ravi
Head of Product, Montecure
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Severe p99 latency + "token decode" errors since v4b + Q4 quant switch

Ravi — thanks for the heads up and the samples. We’re escalating to a triage immediately. I’ve looped in Priyom (infra/serving) and Sergio (CS) to run a fast investigation and propose a short mitigation plan.

Immediate actions: 
- Priyom: can you validate whether the Q4 quant profile is causing decode stalls for long sequences and whether a rollback to v4a is available now?
- Sergio: I’ll coordinate comms and a customer-facing timeline; please prepare a short note for execs if we need credits.

We’ll start with a rollback test on a canary and report back within 60–90 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 May 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Severe p99 latency + "token decode" errors since v4b + Q4 quant switch

Triage notes (initial):
- Reproduced the p99 spike on our internal sig test using the same payloads you provided.
- Root cause hypothesis: the Q4 quant profile used with v4b reduces precision on a few attention kernels resulting in sporadic decode stalls for sequences >512 tokens. The stalls bubble up as token alignment errors and cause backpressure on scheduler leading to CPU/GPU skew and higher p99.
- Observed additional GPU memory pressure that increases GC events on the runtime in a narrow traffic distribution.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Rollback Montecure to v4a (non-quant or previous qprofile) — fastest, low risk; we can push a rollback to your fleet within ~90 minutes after approval.
2) Temporarily reduce max_batch_size and enable the new prefix-cache warm-up patch (reduces cold-start stalls) — low risk, buys ~30–60 mins while rollback completes.
3) Keep v4b and force fallback to the higher-precision attention kernels for sequences >512 via routing rule — medium complexity, ~3–4 hrs to validate.

My recommendation: start with (2) immediately, kick off rollback (1) as parallel path. I’ll open INFR-1324 for the follow-up investigation and collect heap/traces for a full postmortem.

Attachments: extracted trace (error-trace-1.txt) inside the Jira ticket.

— Priyom
Staff Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Severe p99 latency + "token decode" errors since v4b + Q4 quant switch

Ravi — quick update and proposed next steps: 

Summary of what we saw:
- After rolling v4b + Q4 (yesterday), your p99 latency and token-decode errors increased on long sequences. Our infra team reproduced the behavior and traced it to quant-related attention kernel precision reductions that can cause intermittent decode stalls.

What we’re doing now (timeline):
- 10:10 PDT: Enable prefix-cache warm-up + reduce max_batch_size to reduce immediate backpressure (low-risk).
- 10:45 PDT: Begin an automated canary rollback of Montecure traffic to v4a (previous model variant). Canary will validate for 30 minutes.
- 11:30 PDT: If canary looks good, we will roll the remainder of your traffic back to v4a (expected completion by ~12:00 PDT).

Customer-facing mitigations: 
- If rollback completes as planned, we expect p99 to return to baseline and errors to drop within 10–15 minutes post-rollout.
- We’ll produce a postmortem and a permanent mitigation plan (either an updated qprofile or a routing rule to avoid the precision path for long sequences).
- We will calculate credits for the impacted window and share that with you.

Attachments: Montecure impact summary (montecure-impact-summary.xlsx) and the raw CSV sample you sent.

Can you confirm approval to proceed with the rollback path? If you prefer we hold on rollback and only apply the warm-up patch, say so — but our recommendation is to rollback to be safe.

— Tessa
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
